taskPacket.objective: Make every stack-buffer copy these three files perform impossible to overflow, and stop `rec transcribe --out` from destroying the source recording.
instructions: Read FINDING-SYNTH-01, FINDING-SYNTH-02 and section A.6.2 of docs/audits/AUDIT-REPORT.md (and the two surface reports) before editing.

SYNTH-01/SYNTH-02 root cause: `pub fn appendStr` at src/record.zig:616 copies `s` into `buf` starting at `n.*` with no bound check at all. Make the primitive impossible to overrun: check `buf.len - n.* >= s.len` first and return `error{NoSpaceLeft}!void` when it does not fit. Update every caller of the *public* helper (grep for `appendStr`; outside src/record.zig it is used only by src/transcribecmd.zig and src/playback.zig, both in your writeFiles - the other .zig files define their own private copy and belong to other nodes, do not touch them). Propagate the error: command entry points print the command's existing Portuguese usage-error line and return 1.

SYNTH-01 call site: src/transcribecmd.zig:160-163 copies the raw `--out` value into a `[std.Io.Dir.max_path_bytes]u8` stack buffer. Reject an `--out` that cannot fit (`transcribe: caminho de saída longo demais`) on the existing usage-error path; route the `.md` suffix append in the default branch through the same checked helper.

SYNTH-02 call site: src/playback.zig:577-583 (`transcriptPath`) copies `library.stripExt(name)` plus `.md` into an 80-byte stack buffer. Bound it and return `null` when the name does not fit, so the caller keeps reporting 'no transcript' exactly as today.

A.6.2: src/transcribecmd.zig:237 calls `createFile(io, out_path, .{})`, which truncates, with no guard that `out_path` is the recording being transcribed. Before creating the file, refuse when `--out` resolves to the source recording and print `transcribe: --out não pode ser o próprio arquivo de entrada`, returning 1. Resolve the candidate with `std.Io.Dir.cwd().realPathFile` and compare against the already-resolved `abs_buf` recording path; a path that cannot be resolved does not exist yet, so it cannot be the recording.

Add regression tests, inline in the file they test, named exactly: `record.appendStr refuses a buffer too small` (src/record.zig), `transcriptPath refuses a stem that does not fit` (src/playback.zig), `transcribe out path must fit the buffer` (src/transcribecmd.zig), `transcribe out must not be the source recording` (src/transcribecmd.zig). Where a decision lives inside a command function, extract it into a small pure helper (for example the path-equality predicate) so the test calls it directly.

definitionOfDone.text: FINDING-SYNTH-10 is closed: two recorders starting in the same wall-clock second cannot truncate or replace each other's recording.
FINDING-SYNTH-11 is closed: no error path out of `wav.Encoder.finish()` leaves the descriptor open.
FINDING-SYNTH-17 is closed: POSIX WAV files are created owner-only (0600).

taskPacket.objective: Make a recording file impossible to leak, to silently collide with another recorder, or to be world-readable.
instructions: Read FINDING-SYNTH-10, FINDING-SYNTH-11 and FINDING-SYNTH-17 in docs/audits/AUDIT-REPORT.md before editing.

SYNTH-11: src/wav.zig `finish()` sets `self.closed = true` on entry, before the descriptor is actually closed, and every error return (`error.FinalizeFailed`) leaves the fd open; because `closed` is already true, the callers' `abort()` fallback is a no-op too. Close the descriptor unconditionally before returning any error, mirroring `m4a.zig`'s `finish()` (release resources first, inspect the status afterwards). The 4 GiB RIFF-ceiling path (`maxInt(u32) - 36` PCM bytes) fires deterministically; the existing test `wav.test.finish rejects bodies past the 4 GiB RIFF limit` must be extended to assert the descriptor was released, not only that the error came back.
SYNTH-17: src/wav.zig `openNew`'s POSIX branch opens with mode 0o644 while the Windows branch two lines above asks for owner-only. Use 0o600 on POSIX, matching Windows.

SYNTH-10: `create_write_flags` (src/wav.zig) is `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC` with no `O_EXCL`, and the recording name (src/record.zig, `localTimestamp` at one-second resolution) has no uniqueness component, so two recorders started in the same second truncate each other and the later `publish()` rename silently replaces the earlier finished file.

Fix it in two layers: (a) open the temp/`.part` file with `O_EXCL` so a taken name fails loudly instead of truncating another recorder's in-progress audio; (b) on `PathAlreadyExists`, retry with a bounded numeric suffix on the *stem* (`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`, then `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-2`, `-3`, ... up to a small bound) so a second recorder still records instead of failing. Extract the candidate-name computation into a pure, testable function (for example `candidateStem` / `nextStem` taking an existence predicate) rather than open-coding it in the command loop. Keep the published file name shape `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.<ext>` that README.md documents; only update README.md if you change that shape.

Add regression tests inline, named exactly: `wav.finish releases the descriptor when the RIFF ceiling is hit` (src/wav.zig), `recording stems stay unique when the second is taken` (src/record.zig), and keep `wav.create_write_flags` exclusive - assert the flag in a test named `wav.create_write_flags is exclusive` (src/wav.zig).

taskPacket.objective: Stop the Deepgram request from leaking the key through argv, from being steered by --language, from hanging forever, and from buffering an unbounded response.
instructions: Read FINDING-SYNTH-03, FINDING-SYNTH-05, FINDING-SYNTH-07 and FINDING-SYNTH-08 in docs/audits/AUDIT-REPORT.md before editing. All four live in `transcribe()` in src/transcribe.zig.

SYNTH-03 (critical): `Authorization: Token <key>` is passed as a literal `-H` argv element, so the key is readable in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and `ps` for the whole request. Take it off argv: write the header line to a temporary file created 0600 (reuse the 0600 handling `storeKey` already uses in this file), pass it with curl's `@file` header syntax (`-H @<path>`), and delete the file in a `defer`. Do not log the header or the key anywhere.

SYNTH-07: the curl argv has no `--max-time`/`--connect-timeout` and `std.process.run` passes no timeout, so a stalled peer wedges the command forever - `src/update.zig` already bounds its own downloads, so match that. Add an explicit wall-clock bound to the curl argv (and/or `RunOptions.timeout`).

SYNTH-08: neither `stdout_limit` nor `stderr_limit` is set, so a hostile or buggy endpoint can return an unbounded body. Cap the response the way `src/llm.zig` already caps harness output; when the cap is exceeded, fail with the command's existing error path rather than truncating into a silently wrong transcript.

SYNTH-05: `buildListenUrl` (src/transcribe.zig:21-34) splices `--language` straight into the query string, so `en&callback=http://attacker.example/hook` injects a second parameter. Fix it at the source: either validate the value against Deepgram's code syntax (for example `auto`, or `^[a-z]{2}(-[A-Z]{2})?$`) and reject anything else on the command's usage-error path, or percent-encode it before splicing. Pick one, document why in a one-line comment, and keep the fixed parameter order the existing tests pin.

The two existing tests `transcribe.test.listen url splices custom languages verbatim without reordering` and `transcribe.test.listen url keeps the fixed parameter order with explicit Portuguese` encode the old behaviour; update them to the new contract (a behaviour change is expected here) and add tests named exactly: `transcribe authorization never reaches argv` (assert the argv built for a request contains no key material; extract the argv construction into a pure helper if needed), `transcribe listen url rejects an injected language` and `transcribe listen url bounds the language parameter`.

taskPacket.objective: Compare paths instead of strings in `rec format --out`, drain over-length lines in `rec setup`, and bound the two unbounded path builders in `llm.zig`.
instructions: Read FINDING-SYNTH-06, FINDING-SYNTH-15 and section A.6.1 of docs/audits/AUDIT-REPORT.md before editing.

SYNTH-06: src/formatcmd.zig:211-219 guards `--out` against overwriting the source transcript with `std.mem.eql` on raw strings, so `./x.md`, `x.md` and an absolute spelling all slip past and the source is truncated. Compare resolved paths instead (canonicalise both, then compare), and keep the existing Portuguese refusal message and exit code.

SYNTH-15: src/setupcmd.zig `readLine` (around :343-358) stops at `n == buf.len` without consuming the rest of the line, so the leftover bytes answer the *next* prompt. After a truncated read, keep reading and discarding bytes until `\n` or EOF before returning; a line that exactly fills the buffer is truncated, not complete.

A.6.1: src/llm.zig `configDirPath` (:230-254) and `joinPath` (:1132-1142) copy their input into the caller's buffer through the file's private `appendStr` (:1144) with no bound at all. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is attacker-influenced and `configDirPath` runs on almost every command (src/main.zig:106 runs the auto-update check), so a huge value writes kilobytes past a `[std.Io.Dir.max_path_bytes]u8` stack buffer.

Fix A.6.1 the same way the other nodes fix theirs: make llm.zig's private `appendStr` bound-checked (a boolean or error return) and have `configDirPath` and `joinPath` return `null` when the result would not fit. Both already return an optional; every caller in the repository already handles `null` through `if (...) |v|` or `orelse` - verify that with `grep -rn "configDirPath(\|joinPath(" src/` before you rely on it, and if a caller does not, say so in a `missingContext` entry instead of editing a file outside your writeFiles.

Add regression tests inline, named exactly: `format out refuses the same file spelled differently` (src/formatcmd.zig, call the extracted predicate directly), `setup readLine drains an over-length line` (src/setupcmd.zig), `llm.configDirPath refuses a value that does not fit` and `llm.joinPath refuses a value that does not fit` (src/llm.zig).

taskPacket.objective: Make the self-updater verify the release artifact it downloads and stop trusting an unchecked, predictable temp path.
instructions: Read FINDING-SYNTH-09 (the src/update.zig leg) and FINDING-SYNTH-16 in docs/audits/AUDIT-REPORT.md before editing.

SYNTH-09: `apply()` downloads `download_url` from the GitHub Releases API JSON and renames it over the running executable with no checksum, signature or provenance check; this same path runs unattended once a day from `autoCheck`. Add verification that fails closed.

Checksum convention, shared with the workflow/installer node: `release.yml` publishes one extra asset per artifact, named `<artifact>.sha256`, whose entire content is `<64 lowercase hex><two spaces><artifact basename>\n` (the `sha256sum` text format). The updater must locate that sibling asset in the same release JSON (extend `extractRelease`, do not write a second JSON parser), fetch it with the existing `fetch` helper, parse the digest, and compare it against the SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes (`std.crypto.hash.sha2.Sha256`). On any mismatch, missing checksum asset, or unparseable digest: delete the temp file, report failure, and leave the running executable untouched. Never fall back to installing an unverified binary.

Also validate the download URL before fetching it: accept only `https://github.com/feliperun/rec/releases/download/` URLs (reject any other host or scheme), because the JSON is the only input and a rogue/compromised API response must not be able to redirect the updater to an arbitrary host. `extractRelease` is the place to reject it.

SYNTH-16: the temp path is the fixed, predictable `<exe>.update.tmp`, deleted and then recreated by curl with `O_CREAT` but not `O_EXCL`, so a symlink planted there in a shared install directory is followed. Create the temp file exclusively (or use a per-run unique name), and make sure a pre-existing file or symlink at the temp path makes the update fail loudly rather than being followed or clobbered.

Add regression tests inline, named exactly: `update checksum text parses and rejects a mismatch` (a pure parser + compare helper), `update rejects an untrusted download url`, and `update temp path must be created exclusively` (extract the flag choice into a pure helper if the open is not directly callable).

instructions: Read FINDING-SYNTH-04, FINDING-SYNTH-09 (release/installer legs), FINDING-SYNTH-14 and FINDING-SYNTH-19 in docs/audits/AUDIT-REPORT.md before editing.

SYNTH-19: replace every `uses: <action>@<tag>` with the full commit SHA plus a trailing version comment. The exact SHAs were resolved with `git ls-remote https://github.com/<repo> refs/tags/<tag>` on 2026-09-22 and are given so you do not have to guess: actions/checkout@v4 -> 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262, actions/upload-artifact@v4 -> ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02, mlugg/setup-zig@v2 -> d1434d08867e3ee9daa34448df10607b98908d29, googleapis/release-please-action@v5 -> 45996ed1f6d02564a971a2fa1b5860e934307cf7 (this one is an annotated tag; the SHA is its peeled commit). Use them verbatim.

SYNTH-14: `permissions:` is declared once at workflow level in release.yml and applies to every job, so the `build` job carries `pull-requests: write` it never uses. Set the workflow-level permissions to the minimum (contents: read) and give each job only what it needs: `release-please` keeps `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write`, `build` keeps `contents: write` for `gh release upload`.

SYNTH-04: quality.yml downloads `sentrux-linux-x86_64` by version tag, chmods it and runs it, with no integrity check. Pin the expected digest in the step and verify before `chmod`: the v0.5.7 asset's SHA-256, measured locally on this machine from the same URL the workflow uses, is `3237f80fe20d54aad4deefa8a143f0d60543bb5d2d6ad891eb42432f155725a6`. Use `sha256sum -c` (or `shasum -a 256 -c`) with a heredoc and fail the job on mismatch.

SYNTH-09 (release + installers): release.yml must publish a checksum next to every artifact and both installers must verify it. Checksum contract, shared with the src/update.zig node: one asset per artifact named `<artifact>.sha256` whose entire content is `<64 lowercase hex><two spaces><artifact basename>\n` (the `sha256sum` text format).

In release.yml, after staging `dist/<artifact>` and before uploading, generate `dist/<artifact>.sha256` with a step that works on all three runner OSes (the matrix mixes macos-14, ubuntu-latest and windows-latest; python3 is present on all of them, so a short `python3 -c` writing the digest is the portable choice; `sha256sum`/`shasum` are not). Upload both the artifact and its `.sha256` in the same `gh release upload` call.

In install.sh (POSIX sh, `set -eu`): find the `<asset>.sha256` asset URL in the release JSON next to the artifact URL, download it to a temp file, and verify the downloaded binary with `sha256sum` or `shasum -a 256` before `chmod 755`. Fail closed with a clear error and a non-zero exit on a missing checksum, an unparseable digest, or a mismatch. Also require the artifact URL to start with `https://github.com/feliperun/rec/releases/download/`. Keep the script idempotent and shellcheck-clean.

taskPacket.objective: Strip control bytes and escape sequences from every filesystem- or document-derived string before it reaches the terminal.
instructions: Read FINDING-SYNTH-12, FINDING-SYNTH-13, FINDING-SYNTH-18 and section A.6.3 of docs/audits/AUDIT-REPORT.md before editing.

SYNTH-18 (smallest, do it first): src/viewport.zig:45 strips bytes below 32 except tab but not byte 127, while `deck.cleanTitle` strips both. Change the condition to `token[0] < 32 or token[0] == 127`, preserving the tab exception.

SYNTH-12: `library.scan` stores the raw filesystem entry name with no validation, `appendRow` (src/library.zig, around :246-263) copies it byte-for-byte into the row buffer written straight to stdout by `rec list`, and `command_ui.zig`'s `Mode.print` (:9-11) writes unfiltered text to stderr for every command's messages. A file named with `\x1b]0;...\x07` reaches the real terminal on `rec list`, `rec transcribe <bad-selection>` and `rec format <bad-selection>`. Apply one shared filter - the same byte class `deck.cleanTitle` already strips - to the filename before it is stored or before it is copied into the row, and to the text `Mode.print` emits. Prefer one exported helper over two copies; if `deck.cleanTitle` is already public, call it.

SYNTH-13: src/markdown.zig `show()` routes rendered output through the escape-filtering `viewport.Document.set` only when both stdin and stderr are a tty; the `!tty` branch calls `write(io, rendered)` directly, so `rec view notes.md </dev/null` prints raw ANSI/OSC bytes from the document. Filter `rendered` through the same stripping before writing on the `!tty` branch. Do not change the tty branch's behaviour.

A.6.3: src/library.zig:221 declares `var line: [512]u8` and `appendRow` copies the name in unbounded. Today `NAME_MAX` keeps it under the limit, so this is latent, not live - make the copy bounded anyway (truncate or drop the row deliberately) and say in a comment that the bound, not the filesystem, is now the guarantee.

Add regression tests inline, named exactly: `viewport strips DEL like deck.cleanTitle` (src/viewport.zig), `library row filters control bytes in a filename` (src/library.zig), `command output filters control bytes` (src/command_ui.zig), `markdown non-tty output filters escapes` (src/markdown.zig), and `library row never overruns its line buffer` (src/library.zig). The existing `deck.test.a recording title cannot inject terminal commands or extra rows` shows the test style to follow.
